#schema: # Split rule: references/tool-declaration-policy.md
# The heaviest declaration in the corpus, and every record but one is `always`.
# Issue-backed, free-form, and plan-backed all run the same koto loop over the
# same template, differing only in the entry evidence they submit to
# `koto next`, so none of them is a mode. The one mode record is
# `mode:koto-leg`: the koto init entry flags a run needs only under
# --koto-leg, explained with the koto floor below.
# `koto context remove` and `koto context exists` are declared for
# scripts/record-changed-paths.sh, which koto runs as a default_action: it tests
# for impl_base with `exists`, and removes a stale changed_paths.txt with
# `remove` when no base resolves. The context-extraction call site still keeps
# its extracted context under its own key rather than removing one.
# Subcommands and their depended-on flags:
#   init            --template picks the work-on template, --var carries
#                   ISSUE_NUMBER / ARTIFACT_PREFIX
#   next            --with-data submits phase evidence; the whole loop turns
#                   on it. --no-cleanup rides every tick, root or child, so
#                   the terminal tick keeps the session's context instead of
#                   deleting it (references/koto-session-retention.md).
#   workflows       resume lookup, no flag
#   session list    scripts/session-role.sh reads koto's parent_workflow field
#                   from it to tell a root run from a materialized child, the
#                   session_role ci_monitor routes the cascade on
#   status          the Resume step reads is_terminal from it BEFORE ticking, so
#                   a retained finished session is recognised without the tick
#                   that would report it done
#   session cleanup the Resume step's recovery once that record has been read
#   rewind          step back after a failed gate, no flag
#   context add     --from-file for the file-backed keys (context.md,
#                   introspection.md, plan.md); the stdin heredoc form of the
#                   same subcommand takes no flag
#   context get     reads plan.md and context.md in Phase 4, impl_base in
#                   record-changed-paths.sh and has-commits.sh, and pre_pr.md in
#                   check-pre-pr-referents.sh (the referent gates), no flag
#   context exists  the impl_base test in record-changed-paths.sh and
#                   has-commits.sh, no flag
#   context remove  record-changed-paths.sh clears a stale changed_paths.txt,
#                   no flag
#   decisions record  --with-data carries the decision object
# gh reads the issue and drives the PR; git rebases, pushes, and inspects the
# worktree; jq builds the JSON in references/scripts/extract-context.sh.
# scripts/check-staleness.sh, which staleness_check's gate runs, needs the same
# three and nothing else: gh for the issue and its milestone, git log for the
# files the issue names, and jq for the age arithmetic and its report.
# Two flags a line-level extractor will surface here are not koto's and are
# deliberately absent: `--pr-body` names what CI enforces on the authored PR
# body (phase-6-pr.md), and `--session` is extract-context.sh's own argument,
# mentioned on comment lines that also name `koto context add`. The scan drops
# `--session` mechanically, because a shell comment is not a command line; the
# `--pr-body` citation has no mechanical tell and is exempted by name.
# scripts/run-cascade.sh owns the shirabe side of the completion cascade. It
# lives here because /work-on runs the cascade for a standalone issue in its
# cascade_run state, and /execute, which runs it in plan_completion, reaches it
# over a cross-skill path. It probes and re-verifies the chain with
# `validate --lifecycle-chain --format json --mode=ready`, adding
# `--allow-untracked-acs` when WORK_ON_ALLOW_UNTRACKED_ACS=1 suppresses L06; it
# then runs `finalize-chain` over the PLAN's upstream and falls back to
# `transition <plan> Done`. python3 is its portable realpath. /execute declares
# the same records, because it runs the same script and its preflight has to
# find the same tools.
# The scan cannot confirm these from the script's text: run-cascade.sh invokes
# the binary as "$SHIRABE_BIN" rather than as a literal `shirabe`, so a
# line-level extractor never sees the call. These records are therefore the
# description of a call the scan is blind to, which is exactly the omission the
# tool-declaration policy says a declaration cannot catch on its own. Keep them
# in step with the script by hand.
#not-a-call-site
column5: Names what CI enforces on the authored PR body; /work-on authors to the rule and never invokes the check.

#schema: # The koto floor. /work-on needs koto 0.14.1, shirabe's koto minimum
# (scripts/assert-koto-floor.sh). 0.14.0 is the release from which a child's
# result reaches its parent whether or not its tick carried --no-cleanup, which
# is what lets every tick carry the flag. That is behaviour, not a flag, so no
# record below can declare it. The preflight compares koto's version with the
# minimum at load instead (scripts/lib/preflight-minimum.sh), and
# check-koto-entry-floor.yml runs these suites on it.
# `--koto-leg=<request-id>:work-on` adds koto init entry flags. Under it,
# scripts/work-on-open.sh opens the session through the shared
# scripts/koto-open.sh with `koto init --vars-file --attach-live --koto-leg`,
# flags that shipped in koto 0.13.0. That record is `mode:koto-leg`: a run
# without the flag never calls them, so it is not checked at load, and
# SKILL.md's Answering a Caller's Leg section runs `skill-preflight.sh work-on
# --mode koto-leg` before the open. The parity scan cannot see these flags in
# this skill's own files, because the call site is the shared script.
# With the floor past 0.13.0, two things could follow and are left to their
# own change: work-on.md's terminals could get result maps, so a work-on leg
# carries a payload `outcome` like /scope's, /execute's and /deliver's, and
# every /work-on open could go through work-on-open.sh and koto-open.sh,
# retiring the plain `koto init --var` path in SKILL.md, at which point the
# mode:koto-leg record becomes the one `always` init record.
